page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at a dedicated clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core). It features a large 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, though the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU constraint. The stress-ng single-core CPU test achieved a score of 2096.98 (average), while the multi-core CPU test scored 2102.48 (poor). Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 22.83 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 11.59 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations perform moderately well, with gzip compression reaching 30.68 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.86 GB/sec. For lightweight AI workloads, the server achieves 76.28 tokens/sec for text generation using a small 135M LLM model.

From a resource density perspective, the D2ls_v7 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring high single-core clock speeds without massive memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses minimizes overhead for stateless deployments. This server is best suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, single-threaded batch processing, basic web serving (achieving 4.48 GB/sec static web throughput), and small-scale utility applications that do not require high memory capacity or parallel multi-core execution.
